title: KMS re-encrypt window causing API key issuer TTL drift and intermittent 403s across Dedicated/Private
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Several Dedicated and Private customers reported intermittent 403s and authz mismatches during a scheduled KMS re-encryption operation on 2026-03-10. Investigation shows a race between the async re-encrypt job and the API key issuer metadata cache refresh. The re-encrypt updated the active key material, but the issuer verification cache retained an entry with the old key id and a TTL that drifted beyond the expected acceptance window. This resulted in: 1) requests signed with just-rotated key failing verification (403) when hitting a verification node that had not refreshed; 2) in a small number of cases, the fallback acceptance path matched an incorrect tenant mapping and returned tokens scoped to the wrong org for a short period. Impact: Hosted customers unaffected; Dedicated/Private control-plane path that performs customer-managed KMS re-encryption was affected. Scope: ~6 customers reported by support; spike in 403s observed in regional metrics (EU-west, us-central). Hypothesis: The re-encrypt job publishes key metadata asynchronously to the control-plane metadata store, while the local issuer cache on verification nodes uses a time-based TTL plus an opportunistic soft-refresh that can be delayed under load. When the re-encrypt job completed, some nodes still served requests with stale issuer metadata and refused signatures from the new key. Reconciliation paths that attempted emergency acceptance extended trust windows and accidentally matched legacy tenant aliases in a small percentage of requests.
reproduction_steps: 1) Create a Dedicated tenant with customer-managed KMS key. 2) Issue a short-lived API key signed with current key version. 3) Trigger the KMS re-encrypt/rotate operation that atomically replaces key material but publishes metadata asynchronously. 4) Rapidly send signed requests across several verification nodes (curl example below). 5) Observe intermittent 403s from nodes that haven't refreshed issuer metadata; check control-plane metadata store and node-local caches. Example curl: curl -H "Authorization: ApiKey abcdef..." -X POST https://dedicated-api.example.com/v1/generate -d '{"input":"ping"}'
mitigation: Immediate: paused the async re-encrypt job and forced a synchronous metadata publish + cache invalidation across verification nodes. Short term rollback: re-encrypt was rolled back to previous key material for the affected tenants while we stabilized cache behavior. Communication: Notified impacted customers and created a temporary routing rule to favor freshly-synced verification nodes for affected tenants.
current_next_steps: 1) Implement a synchronous metadata publish-and-ack step in the re-encrypt workflow so issuance is gated until all verification nodes acknowledge the new key id. 2) Add a short-term cache-coordination signal (pub/sub) to proactively invalidate issuer caches when rotation happens. 3) Add deterministic tenant-binding checks to fallback acceptance path to prevent cross-tenant mapping during transient windows. 4) Add e2e test harness that simulates re-encrypt + concurrent requests. 5) Schedule a canary rollout for the fix on Dedicated clusters next week.
